articles.title: How to Handle API Rate Limits in Python Like a Pro (with Exponential Backoff)
articles.excerpt: If you are building applications that rely on external APIs (like OpenAI, Gemini, GitHub, or even just fetching job data), you have probably run into the dreaded 429 Too Many Requests error. When I wa…
articles.body: If you are building applications that rely on external APIs (like OpenAI, Gemini, GitHub, or even just fetching job data), you have probably run into the dreaded 429 Too Many Requests error. When I was building my AI backend, my server kept crashing because I was hammering the Gemini API too fast. If you just write a try/except block and instantly try again, you will get banned. You need Exponential Backoff. Here is how it works and how to build it in Python. What is Exponential Backoff? Instead of retrying a failed request immediately, you wait a little bit. If it fails again, you wait twice as long. If it fails again, you wait twice as long as that. · Attempt 1 fails -> Wait 1 second. · Attempt 2 fails -> Wait 2 seconds. · Attempt 3 fails -> Wait 4 seconds.

articles.title: I Was Shipping Five Font Files. One Variable Font Replaced Them All.
articles.excerpt: Open the network tab on a site with a half-decent type system and count the font requests. Four is normal. Six isn't rare. Every one of them is a separate .woff2 file for a separate weight — Regular,…
articles.body: Open the network tab on a site with a half-decent type system and count the font requests. Four is normal. Six isn't rare. Every one of them is a separate .woff2 file for a separate weight — Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold — sitting in the critical path before the browser can paint text in anything but a fallback font. Our design system had five: four weights plus a bold italic for pull-quotes. Nobody had decided that on purpose. It accumulated — a designer added Semibold for one component, Bold Italic followed for another, and eighteen months later the font folder looked like a weight had been added every time someone liked how it looked in Figma. The fix everyone reaches for first When this shows up in a performance audit, the fix is almost always the same: cut weights.

articles.title: The Second Deployment Is the Product
articles.excerpt: Originally published at Trida AI. The most expensive sentence in our line of work is "we've done this before." Said loosely, it means somebody on the team remembers a similar project. Said properly, i…
articles.body: Originally published at Trida AI . The most expensive sentence in our line of work is "we've done this before." Said loosely, it means somebody on the team remembers a similar project. Said properly, it should mean something you can point to: a shelf of artifacts left over from the last deployment, which the next one starts from. The distance between those two meanings is where forward deployed engineering either becomes a business or stays a run of heroic one-offs. A first deployment is discovery at full price. The team learns what the client's data actually looks like, which approvals really matter, where the workflow breaks on a bad Tuesday. That learning is the most valuable thing the engagement produces, and the most perishable.

articles.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
articles.excerpt: SpaceX just made spaceflight history, catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket when it returned to Earth. But Starship still has some pretty big boxes left to check.
articles.body: Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. articles.title: Bluetooth HDT could finally fix wireless audio quality, but there’s still one big problem
articles.excerpt: HDT will be one of the biggest changes to Bluetooth audio in years.
articles.body: News that Bluetooth has officially adopted its new High Data Throughput (HDT) specification should be music to audiophile ears far and wide. And there’s a good chance your future pair of wireless headphones could sound considerably better as a result. If you missed the announcement, Bluetooth HDT extends the capabilities of Bluetooth Low Energy (LE), boosting its maximum physical-layer data rate (PHY, pronounced “fie”) from 2Mbps to a comparatively colossal 7.5Mbps. That’s almost four times the maximum rate of conventional Bluetooth LE, and 2.5 times faster than Bluetooth Enhanced Data Rate (EDR), which tops out at 3Mbps.

articles.excerpt: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize.
articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
articles.excerpt: We're scared of the Xenomorphs again, but Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 knows old-fashioned bug hunts shouldn't be a thing of the past.
articles.body: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years.

articles.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
articles.excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Hele…
articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely .

articles.title: Why did Starship Flight 15 booster abort 'chopsticks' landing catch? SpaceX still investigating (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13) during the Starship Flight 15 test.
articles.body: Update for 3:40 p.m. ET on Nov. 14: SpaceX's Kate Tice provided more information about the booster abort at about 3:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT) on Nov. 14, during the company's Flight 15 webcast. "Early indications are that the booster ended its boostback [burn] early due to a low fuel mass alarm," she said. "The team is still investigating the root cause on that." SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster. The giant Starship rocket , a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight.
